paragraphs: Friend, here is what this whole chapter is ringing about. The LORD says, "Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 20:7) The heavy laws are not random rules piled up to scare people. They show how seriously God takes the difference between what is His and what is not.

Notice how He says it, too. He says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies you." (Leviticus 20:8) He asks His people to keep His statutes, and He is the One who sets them apart. Then He says, "You are to be holy to Me because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be My own." (Leviticus 20:26) Being holy starts with belonging to Him, and everything else grows from there.

So what does this mean for you, baker? You were never meant to blend in with whatever is going on around you. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you it's something else to be picked out and called His own. This chapter has some of the weightiest words in the book, so hold them with care, and let them point you to the God who holds you.
